questions.question: List the assumptions of perfect competition and explain why the individual business faces a horizontal demand curve, naming everything that line represents.
questions.expected_answer: The assumptions: a very large number of buyers and sellers each too small to influence price; a homogeneous product; free entry and exit; perfect knowledge of all prices; and mobile factors of production with no collusion and no government interference in price. The industry's demand and supply curves set the equilibrium market price, and the individual business must accept it: with identical products and fully informed buyers, asking even slightly more sells nothing, while asking less throws away revenue on units that would have sold at the market price anyway. The business is a price taker whose only remaining decision is quantity. Its demand curve is therefore a horizontal line at the market price, and that single line is at once the demand curve, the average revenue curve (every unit sells at the same price) and the marginal revenue curve (each extra unit adds exactly the price): D = AR = MR = P.

questions.question: Explain how a perfectly competitive firm chooses its output and reaches a verdict on profit or loss, including when a loss-making firm should shut down.
questions.expected_answer: Output is chosen where marginal revenue equals marginal cost with MC rising — here, where the rising MC curve cuts the horizontal price line. Every unit before the crossing adds more revenue than cost; every unit past it costs more than it earns, so production stops exactly at the crossing. The verdict comes from average cost at that output. Normal profit — the minimum needed to keep the entrepreneur in the industry, the opportunity cost of capital and enterprise — is built into the cost curves, so when price equals AC the firm breaks even in the economic sense. When price exceeds AC the firm earns economic (supernormal) profit — the rectangle between the price line and AC, per-unit surplus times output (e.g. price R20, AC R17, output 150 gives R450). When price is below AC the firm makes an economic loss. In the short run it should still produce if price covers average variable cost, since fixed costs such as rent are owed regardless and each unit sold then contributes toward them; if price falls below minimum AVC every unit deepens the loss and the firm shuts down. Its supply curve is therefore the rising MC curve above minimum AVC.

questions.question: Describe the long-run outcome of a perfect market and explain how South Africa's competition institutions try to move real markets toward that outcome.
questions.expected_answer: Economic profit attracts entry: supply shifts right and price falls; losses cause exit: supply shifts left and price rises. The process settles where price just touches minimum average cost, so every firm earns normal profit only, with price equal to marginal cost (allocative efficiency — resources follow consumers' wishes) and output at minimum average cost (productive efficiency). Perfect competition alone delivers both, which makes it the benchmark. Because real markets fall short, the Competition Act of 1998 established the Competition Commission, which investigates mergers, cartels and whole markets; the Competition Tribunal, which adjudicates and can block or condition mergers and fine firms up to ten percent of annual turnover; and the Competition Appeal Court, which hears appeals. The Act targets horizontal collusion such as price fixing, market division and bid rigging (South African examples include bread-price fixing and stadium construction bid rigging), vertical restrictive practices such as minimum resale price maintenance, abuse of dominance such as predatory pricing, and anti-competitive mergers — with merger decisions also weighing the public interest in jobs, small business and ownership spread. In model terms, collusion turns many price takers into one price maker, restricting output and lifting price above marginal cost; competition policy restores by law the discipline that many rivals and free entry provide automatically in the model.
